_README: This file exists because check 5 was promoted to BLOCKING on 2026-09-02, and a
blocking gate with no way to record a justified exception refuses correct code
forever -- which is how a gate gets switched off. Every other gate in this repo
has the same escape hatch (SAIRN_SEED_GATE=off) and the same rule about it: use
it deliberately and say so out loud. This is that, made specific and reviewable
THE BAR FOR AN ENTRY. An exemption is a claim that the checker is WRONG about
this finding -- not that the finding is inconvenient, not that it is low
priority, and not that somebody will get to it. A finding that is real and
unfixed belongs in SAIRN-BACKLOG.md, not here.
Every entry carries: the file, the exact finding id, the code (R1/R2/R3), a
reason a reader can check against the source, and the date. An entry that no
longer matches a real finding is reported as STALE by --check-exemptions, so
this file cannot quietly accumulate justifications for code that has moved on.

exemptions.name: sairn-voice-btn
exemptions.reason: The stub is LOAD-BEARING and the file says so at the injector (search 'the sairn-voice-btn placeholder stub stays in place on purpose'). Feature 7's voice module is superseded by the visualizer's own mic controls; the empty stub is the thing making injectVoiceButton() return early, and deleting it makes the page grow a SECOND redundant mic button one level up in the DOM. That was verified in a real browser, which is the only reason it was caught -- from source alone it reads as a missing feature rather than a superseded one. The checker's rule is right in general and wrong here.

exemptions.name: sairn-lock-overlay
exemptions.reason: No longer a collision. saLockScreen() used to early-return on getElementById('sairn-lock-overlay'), which the static stub always satisfied -- that was a real defect and the lock screen had never rendered. Fixed 2026-09-01: it now REUSES the stub and keys 'already showing' on a data-sa-locked attribute the stub does not carry. The id is still both static and JS-touched, so the checker's pattern still matches, but the short-circuit it is looking for no longer exists. Verified by driving the lock screen in a browser.
